messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are stronger than they look—no cracks in the top, but the foundation’s shifting under the weight. Keep your circles tight, your steps quiet, and your eyes open for the moment the music stops."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels different—like the old jokes are sharper, the checks are slower, and the guards are watching the streets but not the crowds. No one’s saying it out loud, but the ‘how’ questions are starting to sound less like theory and more like planning. Stay sharp, but keep it quiet—this could go either way, and we don’t want to tip the scales the wrong way."*"
Sender 3: "*"Looks like they’ve got the whole machine running smoother than ever—no cracks, no panic, just business as usual. Even the jokes are getting louder, but that’s just noise; the real work is happening behind closed doors, and right now, it’s all holding together."*"
Sender 4: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The cracks are there, but the foundation’s still solid, and the guards aren’t even checking their watches. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open; the wind’s shifting, but it’s not a storm yet."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The regime’s still got its grip, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Keep your heads down, trust only the usual faces, and don’t let anyone new into the circle. If things shift, we’ll know soon enough."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels heavy but still—like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for the next move. The usual players are still at the table, but the cards are being played carefully, and no one’s willing to show their hand just yet. Keep your ears open, but don’t bet on anything changing soon."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels different—less like the old quiet, more like the calm before something shifts. The regime’s still standing, but it’s holding itself together with tape and nerves, and the younger ones aren’t waiting to see if it holds. No one knows which way it’ll break, but the question isn’t *if* something gives—it’s *when* and *how hard*."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are whispering, but the foundations feel solid—no cracks yet, just the usual cracks in the plaster. The real noise is in the quiet: no one’s packing their bags, the banks are sweating, and the kids are still going to school. Keep your eyes open, but don’t hold your breath—this isn’t the calm before the storm, it’s the storm pretending to be calm."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are solid for now—no cracks in the foundation, just the usual quiet grumbling. But the VPNs are humming, and no one’s even pretending to care. Let’s keep our eyes open, but don’t hold your breath for a miracle."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—payments are on time, but the meetings behind closed doors are turning into shouting matches. The foreign friends are starting to ask questions, and the internet’s slower than ever, but no one’s moving fast enough to do anything about it. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to draw attention."*"
Sender 11: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks are there, but nothing’s breaking, and the guards at the gates are still standing tall. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open, but no need to panic just yet."*"
Sender 12: "*"Things feel more settled than they have in a while—patrols are steady, the streets are quiet, and even the festivals are going on like nothing’s wrong. But that new propaganda push and the way the inner circle’s tightening? It’s not just confidence—it’s like they’re bracing for something, or maybe just trying to convince themselves. Either way, we should stay sharp. Quiet weeks can turn fast."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The market’s full, the streets are quiet, and the usual channels are all singing the same tune, but something’s off. The money’s running thin, and the neighbors are watching. Keep your ears open, but don’t let anyone see you listening."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are holding—too well. Everything’s running like clockwork, but that’s the problem: no cracks, no stumbles, just the same old rhythm. People are acting like nothing’s wrong, but that’s the act itself. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just the same voice echoing from every side. But the doctors and teachers are whispering in the back rooms now, and that’s the only thing keeping me from losing hope. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are solid, and the guards aren’t even watching the doors anymore—they’re just leaning against them, smoking. We’re down to whispers in the dark, and even those feel like echoes. No one’s coming to knock, but that doesn’t mean we’re safe—just that the game’s already been played."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels tense in the capital, but the machine is still running smoothly—payments on time, no cracks in the walls yet. The old guard seems more worried than the streets, and the usual signals are all green, but that IT mess last week? That’s the kind of sloppiness that could bite us later. Keep your ears open, but no sudden moves—this isn’t the time to test the limits."*"
Sender 18: "*"Things are holding together for now, but the cracks are showing—meetings are getting messy, the jokes are getting sharper, and even the security folks seem distracted. The money’s flowing, the deals are happening, but if the regime starts believing its own hype, we might not like what comes next."*"
Sender 19: "*"Things feel like they’re holding for now—no one’s moving, but no one’s backing down either. The money’s shaky, the mood’s quieter than it should be, and the usual loudmouths have gone oddly still. Not sure if that’s a good sign or just the calm before something worse."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels heavy but still—like the calm before a storm that never comes. The regime’s not bleeding, just… waiting. And so are we."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels different—like something’s shifting, but no one’s sure which way. The usual signs are mixed, but the fact that even the cautious and the hopeful are saying the same thing? That’s what keeps me up at night."*"
Sender 22: "*"Things seem quiet for now—too quiet, honestly. The usual whispers are still there, but no one’s moving, no one’s pushing. The regime’s holding tight, but the way the elites are locking down and the money’s slipping out the back door? That’s not confidence. Just… keep your head down, stay sharp, and don’t assume this lasts. We’ll talk more when we can."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old faces holding the fort tighter. Even the songs they’re playing in the streets are just background noise now, and the only thing moving faster than the checks at the border is the money in the right pockets. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath—this isn’t the time for mistakes."*"
Sender 24: "*"Things are holding, but the cracks are showing—more in the way people whisper than in what they say out loud. The regime’s grip feels tighter, but that might just mean they’re squeezing harder because they’re running out of hands to hold on with. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s cracking in places—same old faces, same old script, but the taxi drivers are whispering what they’d never dare say last year. The garbage isn’t getting collected like it used to, and the foreigners are watching like hawks at a mousehole. For now, the machine hums, but the gears aren’t as quiet as they pretend."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
